findings.issue_text: src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py:11 — MetricAlertDetectorHandler` now subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler` via `pass` but implements none of its abstract members (`counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, `build_occurrence_and_event_data`), so it is still an abstract class; instantiating it (e.g. `Detector.detector_handler` doing `group_type.detector_handler(self)` for any detector with type `metric_alert_fire`, which is registered via `MetricAlertFire.detector_handler = MetricAlertDetectorHandler`) will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class ...` at runtime.

src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py:11 — MetricAlertDetectorHandler(StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]): pass` leaves `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and the new `build_occurrence_and_event_data` abstract methods unimplemented, so `Detector.detector_handler` (src/sentry/workflow_engine/models/detector.py:86) will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class` for any `metric_alert_fire` detector; no test instantiates this handler or exercises a detector of this type, so the PR ships this path completely broken with zero coverage.

src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py:243 — test_state_results_multi_group_dupe` was deleted along with the duplicate-group-key detection/logging code, but no replacement test documents or asserts the new silent "last write wins" behavior when `evaluate_group_key_value` results collide on `group_key` in `results[result.group_key] = result`; this is a behavior change (log-and-skip -> silent overwrite) shipped with zero coverage in either direction.

src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py:11 — MetricAlertDetectorHandler(StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]): pass` no longer satisfies the ABC now that `StatefulDetectorHandler` has four abstract members (`counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and the newly-added `build_occurrence_and_event_data`); it is assigned as `detector_handler` on `MetricAlertFire`, so `Detector.detector_handler` will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class` the moment a detector of that type is evaluated, making this dead/broken code masquerading as a working handler.

src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py:10 — The comment "TODO: This will be a stateful detector when we build that abstraction" is now stale/misleading since `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` already inherits from `StatefulDetectorHandler` in this diff, so the TODO reads as if the class is still a plain (non-stateful) handler.

src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py:60 — Switching `process_detectors`/`evaluate` from list to `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]` silently removes the previous explicit duplicate-group-key detection and `logger.error` call, replacing it with implicit last-write-wins dict overwrite; a genuine bug class (a handler emitting two results for the same group_key) that used to be logged is now invisible to future maintainers.

src/sentry/workflow_engine/models/detector.py:3 — import builtins` is added solely to write `builtins.type[GroupType]` in the `group_type` property's return annotation; the file already has `from __future__ import annotations` at the top, so the annotation is never evaluated at runtime and plain `type[GroupType] | None` would work identically without the extra import, making the `builtins` import unnecessary indirection.

tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py:36 — MockDetectorStateHandler.build_occurrence_and_event_data` delegates straight to `build_mock_occurrence_and_event`, the same helper every test calls to compute its *expected* occurrence/event_data; using one function as both the test double's production logic and the assertion oracle makes comparisons tautological for that code path and means any future behavior change must be edited in exactly one shared place without any test able to catch a divergence, hiding real coupling behind a "helper".

src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py:126 — Changing `evaluate()`'s return type from `list[DetectorEvaluationResult]` to `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]` ripples through `DetectorHandler.evaluate`, `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate`, `process_detectors`, and every test mock/assertion, but the only behavior gained (de-duplication by group_key) was already implicit since `evaluate()` iterates a `group_values` dict that is itself keyed uniquely by group_key — a narrower change (e.g. keeping the list and building the lookup dict only where needed, in `process_detectors`) would have achieved the same de-dup without the pervasive signature churn.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py:11 — MetricAlertDetectorHandler(StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]): pass` leaves `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and the new `build_occurrence_and_event_data` abstract methods unimplemented, so `Detector.detector_handler` (src/sentry/workflow_engine/models/detector.py:86) will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class` for any `metric_alert_fire` detector; no test instantiates this handler or exercises a detector of this type, so the PR ships this path completely broken with zero coverage.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py`, `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` was changed from a concrete `DetectorHandler` (with an `evaluate` implementation) to `StatefulDetectorHandler[...]` with only `pass`. In `src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py`, `StatefulDetectorHandler` defines abstract methods `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and the newly added `build_occurrence_and_event_data` (and still has an abstract `evaluate` in the base `DetectorHandler` contract, implemented by `StatefulDetectorHandler` but dependent on those hooks). Therefore `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` remains abstract and will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class` if `Detector.detector_handler` returns it and code attempts to instantiate it. The diff’s tests only instantiate a fully implemented `MockDetectorStateHandler`, and nothing covers `MetricAlertDetectorHandler`, so this broken instantiation path would ship untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py:243 — test_state_results_multi_group_dupe` was deleted along with the duplicate-group-key detection/logging code, but no replacement test documents or asserts the new silent "last write wins" behavior when `evaluate_group_key_value` results collide on `group_key` in `results[result.group_key] = result`; this is a behavior change (log-and-skip -> silent overwrite) shipped with zero coverage in either direction.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the duplicate-group-key detection in `process_detectors` because the handler API changes from returning a `list[DetectorEvaluationResult]` to returning a `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]` (see `DetectorHandler.evaluate` signature and `process_detectors` loop over `detector_results.values()`). In the new `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate`, iteration is over `group_values.items()` where `group_values` is a `dict[str, int]`, so duplicate group keys cannot occur at that stage (a dict cannot contain the same key twice). The deleted test `test_state_results_multi_group_dupe` relied on a `group_keys` list containing duplicates; that input path is removed/replaced by `group_vals` dicts in tests. Therefore the claimed new "silent last write wins" collision behavior in `results[result.group_key] = result` is not a behavior change that can be exercised given the new dict-based inputs shown in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `DetectorHandler.evaluate`/`process_detectors` to use a `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]` instead of a list, and removes the explicit duplicate `group_key` detection/logging block in `process_detectors` (the `detector_group_keys` set + `logger.error(...)` is deleted). In `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate`, results are accumulated via `results[result.group_key] = result`, which will silently overwrite if the same key is produced more than once during construction. While the new API makes duplicates less representable at the return boundary (a dict can’t contain duplicates), the previous explicit diagnostic is indeed gone and the prior dupe test was removed, making accidental overwrites harder to notice.

adjudication.rationale: In `tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py`, `MockDetectorStateHandler.build_occurrence_and_event_data(...)` directly returns `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(self, ...)`, and many assertions also compute the expected `(occurrence, event_data)` by calling that same `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(...)` helper (e.g., in `test_state_results`, `test_state_results_multi_group`, `TestEvaluate.*`). This means the handler’s occurrence-building behavior and the test’s expected values share the exact same implementation, making that path largely self-fulfilling/tautological and reducing the test’s ability to detect regressions if the occurrence/event schema or fingerprint logic changes in one place.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py:126 — Changing `evaluate()`'s return type from `list[DetectorEvaluationResult]` to `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]` ripples through `DetectorHandler.evaluate`, `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate`, `process_detectors`, and every test mock/assertion, but the only behavior gained (de-duplication by group_key) was already implicit since `evaluate()` iterates a `group_values` dict that is itself keyed uniquely by group_key — a narrower change (e.g. keeping the list and building the lookup dict only where needed, in `process_detectors`) would have achieved the same de-dup without the pervasive signature churn.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes the abstract `DetectorHandler.evaluate` signature and all implementations/usages from returning a `list[DetectorEvaluationResult]` to a `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]` (e.g., `process_detectors`, `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate`, and multiple tests/mocks). That is a pervasive API/typing churn with broad ripple effects. However, the finding’s claim that the *only* behavior gained is de-duplication that was already implicit is only true for `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` (it iterates `group_values: dict[...]`), not necessarily for arbitrary `DetectorHandler` implementations; previously `process_detectors` explicitly guarded against duplicate `group_key`s in the returned list. Still, the architectural/scope concern about changing the public handler contract vs doing de-duping locally is a specific, diff-grounded review issue and not a direct correctness defect.
